title: Project Success
body:
A project is successful when it is delivered **on schedule, within budget, and meeting the
requirements**. Not when the code runs. Working software that arrived a year late, or that
does something adjacent to what was asked for, is a failed project with a working artefact
in it.

That definition is why [[Software Requirements Analysis]] gets a whole phase. "Meeting the
requirements" is only measurable if the requirements were written down and reviewed, which
is what [[Specification]] and [[Review]] are for. A project with vague requirements cannot
fail this test, and cannot pass it either.

The common failure modes are all upstream of the code:

- requirements that were never pinned down, so "done" is a matter of opinion
- scope that grew after the schedule was fixed
- estimates made at the point of least knowledge, then treated as commitments
- a user who first sees the system at delivery, which [[Agile]] exists to prevent

[[Metrics]] is the attempt to measure any of this before the project is over. Related:
[[Projects in software engineering]].
